findings.reason: the plan's own convention carries each implementable section with a `/reckon-build ... §N` followup (f-awcwyh-016 to 020); without two, the roadmap has nothing to schedule for §20 and §21 and their relationships are unstated.
findings.text: §20 and §21 joined `plan-section-declarations` as `implementable` and are the only work left on the plan, yet no followup carries either: the list ends at `f-awcwyh-020` (:1790), whose outcome for §19 reads "No open section remains on this plan", and the new sections are absent from `plan-section-depends-on` (:31) even though §20 writes `reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py`, the module §2 holds and whose test files its done-when runs — the same edge shape this plan's §18 gained depends-on for. Nothing in the followups or the depends-on map records that the plan has two undispatched sections, so it reads as complete while its last two deliverables have no invocation.

findings.text: §20 attributes the walk to run `r-20261023T120024426977-review-of-an-exited-review-with-a-filed-record-reads-complete`, and no directory resolves at `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<that id>`; the record the section describes is `r-20261023T120024426977-review-of-an-exited-review-with-a-filed-record-reads-complete-a9888a470824`, the only entry matching the prefix, and §19 of this plan was already repaired for the identical defect.

findings.reason: the sentence mis-explains the motivation, but the deliverable's rule (report a separation finding for an item whose whitespace splits into declared paths, and quote each stray path) is unaffected, so an implementer is not sent down a wrong path.
findings.text: §21 says "The finding joins stray paths with `, `, so a single parsed path prints exactly like three paths", but `reckon/crew/reports.py:2600` composes the message as `", ".join(stray)`, so three strays print comma-separated and a single space-joined item does not — the join is the one feature that distinguishes three strays from one, and the observed refusal (space-separated, no comma) is evidence of one item rather than of an indiscernible message.
